title: Job Application and CV / Ɛbɔkraho ne CV
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka 'mɛyɛ 25 awɔfoɔ' anaa 'mɛyɛ Tourism foforo', nanso wɔ English, kyerɛwfo no susuw: yɛnka 'to have' ne mmoa a wɔde kyerɛw wɔ 'in' anaa 'from'. Sɛe nso wɔ 'experience' (entumi nka 'experiences' wɔ mfonini a ɛyɛ den no mu) ne sɛnkyerɛnne a ɛdi kan no ho. Fa 'me dedico a' si 'I dedicate myself to' nti, efisɛ ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ fɔm; wɔ English no, wɔka 'I work as' anaa 'I am responsible for'.
rule: Saa ɛbɛka wo nkɔso wɔ English a ɛyɛ B1: 1) Fa present simple kyerɛkyerɛ wo nkɔso a ɛyɛ nea ɛte: 'I work as a...' (Mɛbɔ wɔ...), 'I am responsible for...' (Mɛyɛ ahwɛyɛho...). 2) Sɛ ɛyɛ nkɔso a ɛda no, fa 'used to' anaa past simple: 'I used to work at...' / 'I worked at...'. 3) Fa 'have' kyerɛ wo din ne sɛ wo wɔ hɔ: 'I have five years of experience' (Mɛyɛ five years of experience). 4) Fa sɛnkyerɛnne no maa din no: 'I have strong communication skills' (entumi nka 'skills strong'). 5) Fa 'in' maa mfonini ('experience in hospitality'), 'at' maa company ('at a hotel'), ne 'as' maa din ('as a manager'). 6) Wɔ CV no, wɔfa bullet points ne verb wɔ past anaa present, entumi nka sentences a wɔatwa.

title: Discussing current events / Kasa nkyerɛkyerɛ ne nnwom a ɛyɛ akyi
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyerɛ yɛnka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a. Wɔ English, ɛsɛ wɔka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a (e.g. 'has happened') ne ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a (e.g. 'happened'). Anaa, ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a (e.g. 'is happening') wɔ English so wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a ɛyɛ akyi. Ɛyɛ a wɔde 'está pasando' kaa 'is happening' na ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a ɛyɛ akyi, na ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a ɛyɛ akyi.
rule: Saa wɔka nkyerɛkyerɛ wɔ English wɔ B1: 1. Ka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a (have/has + past participle) ma wɔkasa nkyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ akyi biara: 'Scientists have discovered a new planet.' 2. Ka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a ma wɔkasa nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔde time specific: 'They announced the result yesterday.' 3. Ka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a ma wɔkasa nkyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ akyi: 'The government is debating the new law.' 4. Ma wɔkasa wo adwene, ka ɛno a wɔde kasa kyerɛw wo a: 'I think', 'In my opinion', 'I believe' a wɔde clause ka. 5. Asɛm a ɛsɛ: 'headline', 'article', 'report', 'according to', 'latest', 'issue'.

translations.tw: Kasa nkyerɛkyerɛ ne nnwom a ɛyɛ akyi

title: Cultural Differences and Misunderstandings / Nnyewfi a wͻ Adwene mma mu
bridge: Wͻ Twi, yɛbɛka yɛn ho adwene wͻ hͻ dͻm hwee, nanso wͻ Gyenman ne Amerikani, wͻ’bɛka wͻn ho adwene wͻ hͻ a wͻ’yɛ adwuma wͻ hͻ a wͻ’bɛyɛ. Adwene mma mu biara a wͻ’bɛyɛ wͻ Gyenman ne Amerikani, wͻ’bɛka asɛm bi wͻ hͻ a wͻ’bɛyɛ sɛ ‘Do you mean...?’ na ɛbɛyɛ a wͻ’bɛyɛ adwuma wͻ hͻ. Sɛ wubetumi a, hwɛ sɛ wubɛka asɛm bi wͻ hͻ a wubɛyɛ sɛ ‘What do you mean?’ na wubɛyɛ adwuma wͻ hͻ.
rule: Sɛ wubetumi a, hwɛ sɛ wubɛka asɛm bi wͻ hͻ a wubɛyɛ sɛ: 1) Kyerɛw wo ho adwene wͻ hͻ a wubɛyɛ sɛ ‘Could you explain that?’ na wubɛyɛ adwuma wͻ hͻ. 2) Kyerɛw wo ho adwene wͻ hͻ a wubɛyɛ sɛ ‘I think’, ‘I feel’, ‘I guess’ na wubɛyɛ adwuma wͻ hͻ. 3) Kyerɛw wo ho adwene wͻ hͻ a wubɛyɛ sɛ ‘Do you mean...?’, ‘Are you saying...?’ na wubɛyɛ adwuma wͻ hͻ. 4) Kyerɛw wo ho adwene wͻ hͻ a wubɛyɛ sɛ ‘I misunderstood’ (na wubɛyɛ adwuma wͻ hͻ). Mfa ‘tener razón’ (to be right, na mfa ‘to have reason’) ne ‘hacer falta’ (to need, na mfa ‘to make lack’).

translations.tw: Nnyewfi a wͻ Adwene mma mu

title: Discussing Environmental Topics / Kasa mu nsɛm nnyinasoɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka dwuma a ɛrekɔ so ara na ɛyɛ akyi, yɛnkyɛ present tense ('yɛbɔɔ') anaa present continuous tense ('yɛrekɔ bɔɔ') a ɛntɛm. Wɔ English, nhyehyɛɛ no yɛ den: present simple ('we pollute') ka dwuma a ɛsɛe anaa nnwuma a ɛyɛ den, na present continuous ('we are polluting') ka dwuma a ɛrekɔ so ara na ɛyɛ akyi. Afe a, wɔ English, sɛ wopɛ ka nsɛm a wubɛyɛ akyi (sɛ 'We are going to reduce waste'), wɔhyɛ 'be going to' anaa present continuous, na wɔ Twi yɛnkyɛ future tense ('yɛbɛbɔ'). Fa akoma ntia so ma 'should' a wɔhyɛ amma hyɛ adwuma, a wɔ Twi yɛnkyɛ 'yɛbɛ'.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ ka kasa mu nsɛm nnyinasoɛ wɔ English a ɛtɔ so ara na ɛyɛ akyi, ehia wo nneɛma yi: 1) Present simple (nnwuma a ɛyɛ den: 'The planet is warming' – na ɛno ara wɔhyɛ present continuous efisɛ ɛyɛ dwuma a ɛrekɔ so; sɛ nnwuma: 'Climate change affects everyone'), 2) Present continuous (dwuma a ɛrekɔ so ara na ɛyɛ akyi: 'Forests are disappearing'), 3) 'be going to' + verb (dwuma a wubɛyɛ akyi: 'We are going to install solar panels'), na 4) 'should' + verb (hyɛ adwuma: 'You should recycle more'). Sonka sɛ wɔ English, present simple tense no wɔhyɛ '-s' wɔ third person singular (he/she/it). Sɛ 'there is/are' (ɛyɛ), sonka sɛ 'there is' wɔ singular, 'there are' wɔ plural. Afe a, hyɛ conectores sɛ 'because', 'so', 'therefore' ma woka nsɛm. Mmom sɛnka sɛ adjectives no wɔhyɛ before noun wɔ English ('renewable energy', na ɛnyɛ 'energy renewable').

concept_examples.text: We are reducing our carbon footprint by using public transport.
concept_examples.translation: Yɛrekɔ reduce yɛn carbon footprint efisɛ yɛhyɛ public transport.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ɑːr rɪˈdjuːsɪŋ ˈaʊər ˈkɑːrbən ˈfʊtprɪnt baɪ ˈjuːzɪŋ ˈpʌblɪk ˈtrænspɔːrt/

concept_examples.text: Climate change affects everyone, but we can still make a difference.
concept_examples.translation: Climate change affect everybody, nanso yɛnnyɛ a yɛbɛyɛ difference.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ əˈfɛkts ˈɛvriwʌn, bʌt wiː kæn stɪl meɪk ə ˈdɪfərəns/

concept_examples.text: If we don't act now, the planet will suffer serious consequences.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ yɛmmu dwuma a, the planet bɛtu nnyinasoɛ a ɛyɛ den.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf wiː doʊnt ækt naʊ, ðə ˈplænɪt wɪl ˈsʌfər ˈsɪriəs ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz/

concept_examples.text: You should replace plastic bags with reusable ones.
concept_examples.translation: Wosuo reuseable bags na wubɛhyɛ plastic bags no ase.
concept_examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd rɪˈpleɪs ˈplæstɪk bæɡz wɪð riːˈjuːzəbəl wʌnz/

common_error.wrong: We are recycle the plastic bottles in our house.
common_error.correct: We recycle the plastic bottles in our house.
common_error.correct_alt: We are recycling the plastic bottles in our house.
common_error.explanation: Errour no fi confusion between present simple na present continuous. Wɔ Twi, 'yɛbɔɔ' nea ɛbɛyɛ a, ɛbɛyɛ dwuma anaa ɛbɛyɛ habit. Wɔ English, sɛ ɛyɛ habit anaa routine, hyɛ present simple ('recycle'); sɛ ɛyɛ dwuma a ɛrekɔ so ara na ɛyɛ akyi, hyɛ present continuous ('are recycling'). Wommfa 'are recycle' – verb no nni '-ing' wɔ continuous tense.

levels.label: Describing Environmental Problems
levels.translation: Kasa mu nsɛm nnyinasoɛ

examples.original: Air pollution is a serious problem in many cities.
examples.phonetic: /ɛər pəˈluːʃən ɪz ə ˈsɪriəs ˈprɒbləm ɪn ˈmɛni ˈsɪtiz/
examples.translation: Air pollution yɛ problem a ɛyɛ den wɔ cities pii.
examples.note: Hyɛ 'is' wɔ general facts. Sonka sɛ 'pollution' yɛ uncountable, entɔ wommfa 'a pollution'.

examples.original: The oceans are getting warmer because of climate change.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈoʊʃənz ɑːr ˈɡɛtɪŋ ˈwɔːrmər bɪˈkɒz əv ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ/
examples.translation: Oceans no rekɔ warm efisɛ climate change.
examples.note: Hyɛ present continuous 'are getting' ma woka process a ɛrekɔ so.

examples.original: There is too much plastic waste in the environment.
examples.phonetic: /ðɛr ɪz tuː mʌtʃ ˈplæstɪk weɪst ɪn ðə ɪnˈvaɪrənmənt/
examples.translation: Yɛnni plastic waste pii wɔ environment no mu.
examples.note: Hyɛ 'there is' wɔ uncountable nouns sɛ 'waste'. Mmomfa 'there are waste'.

examples.original: Deforestation destroys the habitat of many animals.
examples.phonetic: /ˌdiːfɒrɪˈsteɪʃən dɪˈstrɔɪz ðə ˈhæbɪtæt əv ˈmɛni ˈænɪməlz/
examples.translation: Deforestation no destroy animals pii habitat.
examples.note: Hyɛ present simple wɔ general facts. Sonka '-s' wɔ third person: 'destroys'.

levels.label: Talking about Solutions and Actions
levels.translation: Kasa mu solutions na dwuma

examples.original: We are planting more trees in our neighborhood.
examples.phonetic: /wiː ɑːr ˈplæntɪŋ mɔːr triːz ɪn ˈaʊər ˈneɪbərhʊd/
examples.translation: Yɛrekɔ plant trees pii wɔ yɛn neighborhood.
examples.note: Hyɛ present continuous wɔ dwuma a ɛrekɔ so ara na ɛyɛ akyi. 'Plant' ma 'planting'.

examples.original: Our school is going to start a recycling program.
examples.phonetic: /ˈaʊər skuːl ɪz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə stɑːrt ə riːˈsaɪklɪŋ ˈproʊɡræm/
examples.translation: Yɛn school bɛstart recycling program.
examples.note: Hyɛ 'be going to' wɔ future plans. Contract 'is going to' wɔ informal conversation.

examples.original: We should use less electricity to save energy.
examples.phonetic: /wiː ʃʊd juːz lɛs ɪlɛkˈtrɪsɪti tə seɪv ˈɛnərdʒi/
examples.translation: Yɛnsuo electricity bi ma yɛsave energy.
examples.note: 'Should' ma verb base (without 'to'). 'Less' wɔ uncountables; 'fewer' wɔ countables.

examples.original: If everyone recycles, we will reduce pollution.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ˈɛvriwʌn riːˈsaɪkəlz, wiː wɪl rɪˈdjuːs pəˈluːʃən/
examples.translation: Sɛ everybody recycle, yɛbɛreduce pollution.
examples.note: First conditional: 'if' + present simple, 'will' + verb. 'Everyone' yɛ singular.

levels.label: Expressing Opinions and Making Recommendations
levels.translation: Kasa mu opinions na hyɛ adwuma

examples.original: I think that electric cars are a good investment for the future.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ θɪŋk ðæt ɪˈlɛktrɪk kɑːrz ɑːr ə ɡʊd ɪnˈvɛstmənt fɔːr ðə ˈfjuːtʃər/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ electric cars yɛ good investment wɔ future.
examples.note: Hyɛ 'I think that' wɔ opinions. After 'think', conjunction 'that' yɛ optional.

examples.original: In my opinion, recycling should be mandatory in every city.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ əˈpɪnjən, riːˈsaɪklɪŋ ʃʊd biː ˈmændətəri ɪn ˈɛvri ˈsɪti/
examples.translation: Wɔ me hyɛɛ mu, recycling nsɛm bɛyɛ compulsory wɔ cities nyinaa.
examples.note: Hyɛ 'in my opinion' + 'should be'. 'Recycling' yɛ noun, entɔ verb no yɛ singular.

examples.original: The government should invest more in renewable energy sources.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈɡʌvərnmənt ʃʊd ɪnˈvɛst mɔːr ɪn rɪˈnjuːəbəl ˈɛnərdʒi ˈsɔːrsɪz/
examples.translation: Government no nsuo invest wɔ renewable energy sources.
examples.note: Advice with 'should'. Adjective 'renewable' ma before noun.

examples.original: If we don't stop deforestation, many species will become extinct.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wiː doʊnt stɒp ˌdiːfɒrɪˈsteɪʃən, ˈmɛni ˈspiːʃiːz wɪl bɪˈkʌm ɪkˈstɪŋkt/
examples.translation: Sɛ yɛmmu deforestation no ase, species pii bɛextinct.
examples.note: Conditional type 1 with 'if we don't'. 'Species' yɛ singular na ɛyɛ plural.

title: Talking About Technology and Social Media / Kasa kɛmɔ akwan a ɔkɔm de a ɛda so ne media a ɛto so
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkye yɛde ɔkɛse kyɛse ma ka a wɔyɛ de a ɛda so ne media a ɛto so, nanso wɔ English, ahemma a ɛwɔ ɔkɛse kyɛse ne ɔkɛse a ɛteɛ ne de a ɛda so no yɛ den. Enti, wɔ kasa kɛmɔ akwan a ɔkɔm de a ɛda so, akanfo a wɔde Twi kasa kyerɛw wɔde nkyɛnkyɛn a wɔwɔ de a ɛda so ho asɛm, sɛ 'me pɛ sika' anaa 'me pɛ foto no', nanso wɔ English no wɔka sɛ 'I have to click' anaa 'I like the photo' a wɔnnhyɛ 'me' a ɛwɔ hɔ bio. Fa akoma ntɔmmɔso wɔ phrasal verbs (sɛ 'log in', 'sign up') a wɔn asɛm nni Twi ho a wɔde kyɛm a ɛto so de kyerɛw.
rule: Ma woka kɛmɔ akwan a ɔkɔm de a ɛda so ne media a ɛto so wɔ English a ɛte B1 no, hwɛ: 1) De ɔkɛse kyɛse ma ka a wɔyɛ de a ɛda so ne media a ɛto so (I check my phone every morning). 2) De ɔkɛse a ɛteɛ ne ma ka a ɛteɛ ne (I am scrolling through Instagram right now). 3) De mmara a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm ne abɔdeɛ: can, should, must (You should update your password). 4) Phrasal verbs a wɔde kyerɛw pɛn: log in, log out, sign up, turn on, turn off, set up. 5) Asɛm a wɔde 'like' ne 'share' kyerɛw (I like the post, She shared the video). Nya da sɛ wɔ English no wɔnnhyɛ ɛkwan a ɛte 'social media' (I spend time on social media, ɛnnhyɛ 'in the social media'). Enti, ma woka de a ɛda so ho asɛm no, de 'have' (I have a new phone) ɛnnhyɛ 'tengo' a ɛte 'there is'.

concept_examples.translation: Da biara me rekɔ me media a ɛto so no ho.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈjuːʒuəli tʃek maɪ ˈsoʊʃl ˈmiːdiə ɪn ðə ˈmɔːrnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: She is posting a story on Instagram right now.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔbaa no rema ɔhaw a ɛwɔ Instagram so daa.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi ɪz ˈpoʊstɪŋ ə ˈstɔːri ɑːn ˈɪnstəɡræm raɪt naʊ/

concept_examples.text: You should log out of your account on public computers.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ woka wo akontom a ɛwɔ kompyuta a ɛyɛ ɔha a wɔde hyɛ da no so.
concept_examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd lɔːɡ aʊt əv jʊər əˈkaʊnt ɑːn ˈpʌblɪk kəmˈpjuːtərz/

concept_examples.text: Can you help me set up my new laptop?
concept_examples.translation: Womma wo ntɔm ma wosiesie me laptop a ɛyɛ paa no?
concept_examples.phonetic: /kæn juː hɛlp miː sɛt ʌp maɪ nuː ˈlæptɑːp/

common_error.wrong: I am agree with you about social media.
common_error.correct: I agree with you about social media.
common_error.correct_alt: I agree on that point about social media.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, yɛka sɛ 'me pɛ', nanso wɔ English no, 'agree' yɛ ɔkɛse a ɛteɛ ne enti wɔnnhyɛ no wɔ ɔkɛse a ɛteɛ ne ho. Ma wobu akɔnnɔ no, nya da sɛ 'agree' nni 'be' a ɛwɔ so. Ɛkyerɛw a ɛteɛ ne biara ne sɛ wɔka sɛ 'I am agree', nanso a ɛho nhia paa no ne sɛ wɔka sɛ 'I agree'. Ɛno akyi, womma woka sɛ 'I agree with you' (me pɛ wo) anaa 'I agree on that' (me pɛ no).

levels.label: Basic Vocabulary and Phrases for Tech
levels.translation: Asɛm a ɛte kwan a ɔkɔm de a ɛda so ne media a ɛto so

examples.original: I need to charge my phone.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ niːd tə tʃɑːrdʒ maɪ foʊn/
examples.translation: Me pɛ sɛ me si me telefon no.
examples.note: Ɔkɛse 'charge' kyerɛw sɛ wosi telefon no. Wɔ Twi, yɛde 'si' ma ka telefon no, nanso wɔ English no, wɔnnhyɛ 'load' wɔ ɔkɛse yi ho.

examples.original: My laptop is very slow.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ ˈlæptɑːp ɪz ˈvɛri sloʊ/
examples.translation: Me laptop no te soro.
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛ wɔ English no, 'slow' de kyerɛw laptop no a ɛte soro, sɛ Twi ara, nanso ɛmmfa 'late' (daa) akɔto so.

examples.original: Do you have a charger?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː hæv ə ˈtʃɑːrdʒər/
examples.translation: Wohwɛ sii?
examples.note: Asɛm bi a ɛte paa wɔ kasa. Nya da sɛ 'charger' ne sii no, ɛnnhyɛ 'loader'.

levels.label: Describing Online Activities
levels.translation: Kasa kɛmɔ akwan a ɔkɔm de a ɛda so

examples.original: I'm scrolling through my feed.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ˈskroʊlɪŋ θruː maɪ fiːd/
examples.translation: Mema me feed no.
examples.note: Phrasal verb 'scroll through' de kyerɛw sɛ woma ɛkwan no. Wɔ Twi, yɛka sɛ 'ma' anaa 'de scroll', nanso wɔ English no, wɔde 'scroll' sɛ ɔkɛse.

examples.original: She uploaded a new video yesterday.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi ʌpˈloʊdɪd ə nuː ˈvɪdioʊ ˈjɛstərdeɪ/
examples.translation: Ɔbaa no sii video paa baabi aa ɛda no.
examples.note: Wɔ English no, 'upload' de kyerɛw sɛ wosi video; wɔ Twi, yɛde 'sii' anaa 'tɔ' wɔ ɛkwan bi ho. Yɛde ɔkɛse a ɛda no ho kasa.

examples.original: He liked my post and commented.
examples.phonetic: /hiː laɪkt maɪ poʊst ænd ˈkɑːmɛntɪd/
examples.translation: Ɔno pɛ me post no enti ɔde kyerɛw.
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛ wɔ English no, wɔka sɛ 'he liked' (ɛnnhyɛ 'he liked it' sɛ wɔhu) enti ɔkɛse 'like' nni ɔkɛse a ɛteɛ ne sɛ Twi 'ɔpɛ'.

examples.original: Are you following that influencer?
examples.phonetic: /ɑːr juː ˈfɑːloʊɪŋ ðæt ˈɪnfluənsər/
examples.translation: Wohwɛ ɔhaw a ɔwɔ influencer no so?
examples.note: Ɔkɛse 'follow' de kyerɛw wɔ media a ɛto so. Wɔ Twi, yɛde 'hwɛ' anaa 'to', nanso wɔ English no, ɛyɛ ara. Hwɛ sɛ wɔde ɔkɛse a ɛteɛ ne ma kyerɛw asɛm.

levels.label: Discussing Pros and Cons of Social Media
levels.translation: Kasa kɛmɔ akwan a ɔkɔm de a ɛda so ne media a ɛto so a ɛyɛ ne a ɛnyɛ

examples.original: Social media can be addictive.
examples.phonetic: /ˈsoʊʃl ˈmiːdiə kæn biː əˈdɪktɪv/
examples.translation: Media a ɛto so ne mmara bi a ɛwɔ hɔ.
examples.note: Yɛde mmara 'can' ma kyerɛw sɛ ɛyɛ a ɛbɛyɛ. Wɔ Twi, yɛka sɛ 'ɛyɛ a ɛbɛyɛ', nanso wɔ English no, mmara no nni ɔkɛse a ɛho nhia.

examples.original: One advantage is that you can connect with people worldwide.
examples.phonetic: /wʌn ədˈvæntɪdʒ ɪz ðæt juː kæn kəˈnɛkt wɪð ˈpiːpəl ˈwɜːrldwaɪd/
examples.translation: Ahemma bi ne sɛ woma wɔn a wɔwɔ aleɛ ne abien aa wɔwɔ hɔ.
examples.note: Yɛde 'one advantage' ma kyerɛw ahemma bi. Wɔ Twi, yɛka sɛ 'ahemma bi ne sɛ', nanso wɔ English no, ɛyɛ ara.

examples.original: However, it can waste a lot of time.
examples.phonetic: /haʊˈɛvər, ɪt kæn weɪst ə lɑːt əv taɪm/
examples.translation: Nanso, ɛbɛsi wɔn a wɔwɔ aleɛ ne abien aa wɔwɔ hɔ pii.
examples.note: Asɛm 'however' ne kyerɛw a ɛho nhia. Wɔ Twi, yɛde 'nanso'. Nya da sɛ 'waste' kyerɛw sɛ wosi, ɛnnhyɛ 'spend' (si).

examples.original: I think it's better to limit screen time.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ θɪŋk ɪts ˈbɛtər tə ˈlɪmɪt skriːn taɪm/
examples.translation: Mehwɛ sɛ ɛho nhia sɛ wɔsi aleɛ a ɛwɔ ɛkwan no so.
examples.note: Yɛde 'it's better to' + ɔkɛse a ɛnni ahoɔden ma kyerɛw asɛm. Wɔ Twi, yɛka sɛ 'ɛho nhia sɛ wosi', nanso wɔ English no, wɔde 'to limit'.

title: Talking about Education and Studying Abroad / Akwan mu Edwuma ne Adwuma a wɔreba mu
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka ho asɛm a ɛbɛba a, yɛnkyɛ present tense anaa simple future tense ('Mɛkɔ sua', 'Mɛsɔ'), nanso wɔ English, wɔkyɛ present continuous tense a ɛwɔ hɔ ma wɔbɛka ho asɛm a ɛbɛba a wɔda plan aa wɔahyɛ no so ('I am studying') sɛ wɔwɔ hɔ. Enti, ma wo hu a, wɔ English, wɔnnsɛ 'I have 20 years' nanso wɔka 'I am 20 years old'. Sɛ woka ho asɛm a wɔkyerɛ no a, woabɛhu sɛ wɔ English, wɔnntumi de article de kyerɛɛw subjects ne fields of study no mu ('I study mathematics'), nanso wɔ Spanish, wɔde article de kyerɛɛw no mu ('Estudio las matemáticas'). Fa akwan a ɛte saa yi so ma woka te sɛ woara wo ho asɛm.
rule: Sɛ woka ho asɛm a wɔkyerɛ ne sɛ wɔreba mu a, fa: 1. Present simple tense ma woka ho asɛm a ɛwɔ hɔ ne sɛ woka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ routine ('I study every day'). 2. Present continuous tense ma woka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ now ('I am studying for my exam') ne ma woka ho asɛm a ɛbɛba a wɔda plan aa wɔahyɛ no so ('I am going to England next month'). 3. 'Going to' ma woka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ intention ('I'm going to apply for a scholarship'). 4. 'Will' ma woka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ spontaneous decision anaa prediction ('I think it will be a great experience'). 5. Modal verbs sɛ 'can', 'must', 'should' ma woka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ ability, obligation ne recommendation ('You should apply early'). 6. Prepositions: 'study at a university', 'apply for a course', 'major in' (specialize in), 'take an exam'. 7. Subjects names without article ('I like history'). 8. Fa 'abroad' (wɔ mu) without preposition, nanso fa 'to study abroad' anaa 'study abroad' sɛ verb anaa noun.

concept_examples.translation: ɛsɛ sɛ wosɔrekyekye wɔ scholarship no ho berɛ a ɛte paa.
concept_examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd əˈplaɪ fɔːr ə ˈskɒləʃɪp ˈɜːrli/

concept_examples.text: We are going to study abroad next semester.
concept_examples.translation: Yɛbɛkɔ sua wɔ mu afɔno bi ara sem.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ˈɑːr ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈstʌdi əˈbrɔːd nekst sɪˈmestər/

common_error.correct: I am 20 years old and I study at the university.
common_error.correct_alt: I am 20 and I attend university.
common_error.explanation: Error no 'I have 20 years' yɛ literal translation a wɔde Spanish 'tengo 20 años' hyɛ no. Wɔ English, wɔfa verb 'to be' ne age: 'I am 20 years old'. Enti, wɔ English, wɔka 'study at the university' (nnom 'in the university') efisɛ wɔfa 'at' ma wɔkyerɛɛ institution no. Fa akwan a ɛte saa yi so ma woyɛ error a ɛte saa yi no ho nhyehyɛe.

levels.label: Describing your studies
levels.translation: Woka ho asɛm a wɔkyerɛ no

examples.original: I am a student at a university in Madrid.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm ə ˈstuːdənt æt ə ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːrsəti ɪn məˈdrɪd/
examples.translation: Menyɛ student wɔ Madrid university mu.
examples.note: Fa 'at' ma wokyɛ institution a wosua no, nnomm 'in'.

examples.original: I am studying law this year.

title: Talking about Past Trips and Travel Experiences / Kasa mu nsɛm ne nnwim a ɛyɛɛ no ho
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka nsɛm a ɛyɛɛ no ho, yɛnkyea ahyɛ a ɛyɛ ɛkɛ ne ahyɛ a ɛyɛ ɛkɛ daa, na ɛnsɛ sɛ yɛbɛka 'mɛn wɔ' ne 'mɛn no' a ɛbɛka ɛnsɛ no ara nti. Wɔ English mu, ɛnsɛ no te sɛ, na mmara no te sɛ: present perfect (have + past participle) de yɛnka ho nhia a wɔanbɛma no time biara, na past simple (I traveled) de yɛnka ho nhia a ɛyɛɛ wɔ time bi a ɛyɛɛ no ho. Ɛyɛ a wɔbɛka past simple nkyerɛ present perfect sɛ wɔrebɛka 'Have you ever been...?' nti ɛyɛ a ɛbɛyɛ den, efisɛ wɔ Twi mu yɛnka 'has estado' nanso wɔ English mu yɛnka 'have you ever been'. Afe a, wɔ English mu, mmara biara nni ho nhia a wɔde bɛka 'go/went/gone' ne 'see/saw/seen', na ɛno nti, ɛyɛ a wɔde 'been' ne 'gone' bɛyɛ den: 'have been' kyerɛ sɛ wɔfa ne wɔbɛba, na 'have gone' kyerɛ sɛ wɔwɔ hɔ ara.
rule: Sɛ wɔbɛka nsɛm a ɛyɛɛ no ho wɔ English mu wɔ B1 kyrɛ, ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔbɛka two tenses: present perfect (have/has + past participle) ne past simple (verb in past tense). De present perfect ma: 1) nsɛm a ɛyɛɛ no ho a wɔanbɛma no time biara (I have visited Paris), 2) with adverbs like 'ever', 'never', 'already', 'yet' (Have you ever been to Japan?), 3) ho nhia a ɛto n'ani wɔ time bi a ɛyɛɛ no ho na ɛso rɛn (I have lived here for three years). De past simple ma: 1) ho nhia a ɛyɛɛ no ho wɔ time bi a ɛyɛɛ no ho (I visited Paris last summer), 2) with time expressions like 'yesterday', 'in 2019', 'last week', 'when I was a child'. Common irregular verbs for travel: go-went-gone, see-saw-seen, eat-ate-eaten, take-took-taken, fly-flew-flown, ride-rode-ridden, drive-drove-driven, stay-stayed-stayed (regular). Question structure in present perfect: Have/Has + subject + past participle? (Have you ever flown first class?). Short answers: Yes, I have / No, I haven't. In past simple: Did + subject + base verb? (Did you go to the beach?). Short answers: Yes, I did / No, I didn't. With 'ever' and 'never' de present perfect, not past simple: 'I have never been to Mexico' (not 'I never went to Mexico' when it's a life experience). Mma wɔde 'since' bɛma time a ɛyɛɛ no ho (I have visited Spain since 2018 - ɛyɛ den sɛ ɛnni ho nhia a ɛso rɛn), de 'since' ma ho nhia a ɛto n'ani (I have been in Spain since 2018). Ntira sɛ wɔde opinion adjectives (amazing, terrible, wonderful, boring) bɛma 'was/were' wɔ past simple de bɛka nsɛm a ɛyɛɛ no ho ho nhia.

translations.tw: Nsɛm a ɛyɛɛ no ho ne nnwim

title: Talking about habits and routines / Kasa mu nsɛm ne nnwim nea yɛyɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkye English, yɛmfa present simple tense ka kasa mu nsɛm ne nnwim a yɛyɛ, nanso wɔ English mu, present simple tense pɛ ‘do/does’ sɛ yɛbɛma aba ne sɛ yɛbɛhyɛ adwuma. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woakasa mu nsɛm ne nnwim a woyɛ a, woabɛfa ‘do/does’ ma woakasa. Na wɔ Twi mu, yɛmfa ‘no’ ma yɛne ‘do/does’ ma yɛkasa. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woakasa mu nsɛm ne nnwim a woyɛ a, woabɛfa ‘no’ ma woakasa. Na wɔ English mu, adverbials a wɔkyerɛ nsɛm ne nnwim a yɛyɛ (always, usually, etc.) wɔde wɔn fa verb a ɛwɔ hɔ bio, nanso wɔ Twi mu, yɛde wɔn fa verb a ɛwɔ hɔ akyiri. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woakasa mu nsɛm ne nnwim a woyɛ a, woabɛfa adverbials a wɔkyerɛ nsɛm ne nnwim a woyɛ ma woakasa.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woakasa mu nsɛm ne nnwim a woyɛ a, woabɛfa present simple tense. Sɛ ɛyɛ third person singular (he, she, it), woabɛfa -s anaa -es ma verb no (e.g., 'works', 'goes'). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wonee, woabɛfa 'do not' (don't) anaa 'does not' (doesn't) ma verb no. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wohyɛ adwuma, woabɛfa 'do' anaa 'does' ma woakasa, na woabɛfa subject no na verb no akyiri. Adverbials a wɔkyerɛ nsɛm ne nnwim a yɛyɛ (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) wɔde wɔn fa: (1) verb a ɛwɔ hɔ bio (I always drink coffee), (2) verb a ɛyɛ 'to be' akyiri (He is always late), na (3) auxiliary verb ne verb no akyiri wɔ adwuma ne nekyee mu (Do you often exercise?). Exceptions: sɛ 'have' yɛ verb a ɛwɔ hɔ bio, woabɛfa 'have/has' (I have breakfast at 8). Sɛ 'go' ne 'do' yɛ verb a ɛwɔ hɔ bio, third person no bɛyɛ 'goes' ne 'does'. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woakasa nsɛm a ɛyɛ now, woammfa present simple tense; woabɛfa present continuous tense.

title: Making Plans and Invitations / Kɔhwɛ mfatoho ne ahuakwanwa
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛkae ne yɛbɛto so ara ka ho asɛm, yɛnka mfatoho bɛka 'wɔhwɛ a...?' anaa 'ɛnte saa...?', na wɔn sɛm a ɛde pɛn so wɔ Espaniol. Ɛkwan a ɛfata ho a wɔde bɛkae wɔ mfatoho mmra ne sɛ 'hang out' a wɔde yɛe wɔ nnipa a wɔatwa mu kasa mu. Fa akɔntɔa sɛ Twi de anigye kɛse (I'm meeting) maa mfatoho a ɛbɛba akyi, na Espaniol pɛpɛɛpɛ de anigye kɛse (Quedo).
rule: Sɛ yɛbɛto so ara ka ho asɛm a, yɛnka: 'Wɔhwɛ a + ɔkwan?' (formal) anaa 'Wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛ...?' (informal). Sɛ yɛbɛka mfatoho a, yɛnka 'ɛnte saa + ɔkwan?' anaa 'ɛnte saa + ɔkwan?'. Sɛ wopɛ a, ka 'Daabi', 'Ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ', 'Mepɛ sɛ mɛyɛ'. Sɛ wopɛ a, ka 'Mede meho a mɛntumi', 'Maforo, mɛyɛ mfatoho biara'. Sɛ mfatoho a ɛbɛba akyi a, yɛnka anigye kɛse (I'm meeting my friends tomorrow) anaa 'going to' (I'm going to visit my sister). 'Hang out' kyerɛ sɛ wɔde time a ɛyɛ den na wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma wɔ mu. Hwehwɛ sɛ wɔmmusɛm a wɔde bɛkae wɔ Espaniol '¿Quedamos?' sɛ 'Are we staying?', na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛka 'Yɛbɛhyɛ adwuma?' anaa 'Yɛbɛhyɛ adwuma pɛpɛɛpɛ?'

concept_examples.text: Would you like to go to the movies tonight?
concept_examples.translation: Wɔhwɛ a wɔbɛka kuro biosu a ɛbɛba?
concept_examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː laɪk tə ɡoʊ tə ðə ˈmuːviz təˈnaɪt/

concept_examples.text: How about hanging out at the park on Saturday?
concept_examples.translation: ɛnte saa yɛbɛka pae mu wɔ Saturday?
concept_examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ˈhæŋɪŋ aʊt æt ðə pɑːrk ɒn ˈsætərdeɪ/

concept_examples.text: Sure, sounds great!
concept_examples.translation: Daabi, ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ!
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃʊr saʊndz ɡreɪt/

concept_examples.text: I'm afraid I can't make it; I have other plans.
concept_examples.translation: Mede meho a mɛntumi; mɛyɛ mfatoho biara.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪm əˈfreɪd aɪ kænt meɪk ɪt aɪ hæv ˈʌðər plænz/

common_error.explanation: Asɔre no fi asɛm a wɔde bɛkae wɔ Espaniol '¿Quedamos?' a wɔde musɛm a wɔkae wɔ Twi sɛ 'Are we staying?', nanso 'staying' kyerɛ 'ma' anaa 'fa'. Wɔ Twi, sɛ wopɛ a, wɔde 'hyɛ adwuma' anaa 'hyɛ adwuma pɛpɛɛpɛ'. Afei, 'shall' yɛ mfatoho a ɛyɛ den, na 'let's' yɛ mfatoho a ɛyɛ den pɛn.

levels.label: Making Invitations
levels.translation: Kɔhwɛ ahuakwanwa

examples.original: Do you want to grab a coffee sometime?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː wɒnt tə ɡræb ə ˈkɒfi ˈsʌmtaɪm/
examples.translation: Wopɛ sɛ yɛbɛka coffee da bi?
examples.note: 'Grab' yɛ informal a wɔde ka 'ka' anaa 'fa kwan'.

examples.original: Would you like to come to my party on Friday?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː laɪk tə kʌm tə maɪ ˈpɑːrti ɒn ˈfraɪdeɪ/
examples.translation: Wɔhwɛ a wɔbɛba me party a ɛbɛba Friday?
examples.note: Mfatoho yi yɛ den pɛn na ɛte sɛ 'do you want to' pɛ.

levels.label: Suggesting Activities
levels.translation: Kɔhwɛ mfatoho

examples.original: What about watching a series tonight?
examples.phonetic: /wɒt əˈbaʊt ˈwɒtʃɪŋ ə ˈsɪəriːz təˈnaɪt/
examples.translation: ɛnte saa yɛbɛka TV daa a ɛbɛba?
examples.note: 'What about' + ɔkwan yɛ mfatoho a wɔde yɛe wɔ Twi.

examples.original: How about going to the beach this weekend?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ðə biːtʃ ðɪs ˌwiːkˈend/
examples.translation: ɛnte saa yɛbɛka beach a ɛbɛba weekend yi?
examples.note: 'How about' ne 'what about' wɔde yɛe wɔ mfatoho mu.

examples.original: We could hang out after the meeting.
examples.phonetic: /wiː kʊd hæŋ aʊt ˈæftər ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ/
examples.translation: Yɛbɛka pae mu akyi akyi.
examples.note: 'Could' kyerɛ akoma a ɛyɛ den na ɛma mfatoho no yɛ den pɛn.

levels.label: Accepting and Declining
levels.translation: Asoɔ ne afutuo

examples.original: I'd love to, but I'm busy on Sunday.
examples.phonetic: /aɪd lʌv tə bʌt aɪm ˈbɪzi ɒn ˈsʌndeɪ/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mɛyɛ, nanso mɛyɛ adwuma wɔ Sunday.
examples.note: 'I'd love to' kyerɛ akoma, na 'but' de afutuo no.

examples.original: That sounds fun! Let's do it.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt saʊndz fʌn lɛts duː ɪt/
examples.translation: Ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ! Yɛbɛyɛ.
examples.note: 'Let's do it' yɛ mfatoho a ɛyɛ den a wɔde asoɔ.

examples.original: Sorry, I can't. Maybe another time.
examples.phonetic: /ˈsɒri aɪ kænt ˈmeɪbi əˈnʌðər taɪm/
examples.translation: Maforo, mɛntumi. Ebi akyi.
examples.note: 'Maybe another time' de afutuo no yɛ den pɛn na ɛma ɛso bɛyɛ.

title: Giving a short presentation / Kyɛfa kwan so kyɛfa
bridge: Wɔ Hɔwyɛdeɛ mu, yɛbɛka yɛn adwene wɔ anwummerɛ ne wɔ mfatoho mma mu paa. Wɔ Twirifɔdeɛ mu, ma wɔkyerɛkyerɛ deɛ ɛbɛyɛ ne deɛ ɛyɛ anigye wɔ kyerɛw kronkron ne mfatoho mma mu. Ntɛmbua ko ɛha wɔ Twirifɔdeɛ mu na wɔde ɛnkyɛnkyɛn mu kyerɛw ma wɔde 'going to' anaa 'will' kyerɛkyerɛ nneɛma a ɛbɛn na wɔde presente simple kyerɛkyerɛ nneɛma a wɔyɛ, na wɔ Hɔwyɛdeɛ mu biara, yɛde presente anaa nneɛma a ɛbɛn na yɛde mfatoho mma a wɔn ho hia wɔn a wɔn ho hia. Ansa na, wɔ Twirifɔdeɛ mu, wɔde asɛm a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ (sɛ 'firstly', 'in addition', 'to sum up') ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ kwan so kyɛfa, na wɔ Hɔwyɛdeɛ mu, yɛde mfatoho mma sɛ 'en primer lugar', 'además', 'para resumir'.
rule: Ma wɔde kwan so kyɛfa wɔ Twirifɔdeɛ mu, su ɛyi mfatoho: 1) Ma wɔde asɛm kyerɛ ma wɔde asɛm kyerɛ (sɛ 'Good morning, I'm going to talk about...'), 2) Ma wɔde adwene wɔ mfatoho mma mu (firstly, secondly, in addition, however), 3) Ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ (to conclude, in summary). De ɛnkyɛnkyɛn mu ma wɔde kyerɛw ne adwene, na 'going to' anaa 'will' ma wɔde kyerɛw anaa adwene. Fa so wɔde kyerɛw a ɛyɛ den na wɔde asɛm a ɛyɛ den ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. Wɔde kyerɛw ne wɔde kyerɛw sɛ 'Let me start by...', 'Moving on to...', 'To wrap up...'.

concept_examples.text: Good morning, today I'm going to talk about the importance of recycling.
concept_examples.translation: Mema wo a, me bɛka ho asɛm no wɔ ɛpo mu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɡʊd ˈmɔːrnɪŋ təˈdeɪ aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə tɔːk əˈbaʊt ði ɪmˈpɔːrtəns əv rɪˈsaɪklɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: Firstly, recycling helps reduce waste in our cities.
concept_examples.translation: Pa ara, ɛpo mu bɔɔ bɛma yɛn ntɔmwɔ so.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈfɜːrstli ˈriːsaɪklɪŋ helps rɪˈduːs weɪst ɪn aʊər ˈsɪtiz/

concept_examples.text: In addition, it saves energy and natural resources.
concept_examples.translation: Ansa na, ɛbɛma yɛn ntɔmwɔ ne yɛn nnwuma so.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪn əˈdɪʃən ɪt seɪvz ˈenərdʒi ənd ˈnætʃrəl ˈriːsɔːrsɪz/

concept_examples.text: To conclude, we all should recycle more to protect the planet.
concept_examples.translation: Ma me kyerɛkyerɛ, yɛnyina yɛn nyinaa yɛbɔ ɛpo mu ma yɛma ahennwa no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /tə kənˈkluːd wi ɔːl ʃʊd rɪˈsaɪkl mɔːr tə prəˈtekt ðə ˈplænɪt/

common_error.wrong: Good morning, I going to talk about the recycling.
common_error.correct: Good morning, I'm going to talk about recycling.
common_error.correct_alt: Good morning, I'm going to talk about the importance of recycling.
common_error.explanation: Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔde 'to be' kɔ so wɔ 'be going to' mu, ɛfiri sɛ wɔ Hɔwyɛdeɛ mu, wɔbɛka 'voy a hablar'. Wɔ Twirifɔdeɛ mu, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'to be' kɔ so wɔ ɛnkyɛnkyɛn mu ('I am') a wɔde 'going to' kɔ so. Ansa na, wɔ Twirifɔdeɛ mu, wɔmmusɛ 'the' kɔ so wɔ ɛnkyɛnkyɛn mu sɛ 'recycling' (yɛka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ den paa). Ma wɔatwe, bu 'am/is/are' ne mmusɛ 'the' a wɔde kɔ so wɔ ɛnkyɛnkyɛn mu.

levels.label: Opening a presentation
levels.translation: Kyɛfa kwan so kyɛfa

examples.original: Good morning, everyone.
examples.phonetic: /ɡʊd ˈmɔːrnɪŋ ˈevriwʌn/
examples.translation: Mema wo nyinaa a.
examples.note: Asɛm a ɛyɛ den ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'everyone' ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ.

examples.original: I'd like to start by talking about...
examples.phonetic: /aɪd laɪk tə stɑːrt baɪ ˈtɔːkɪŋ əbaʊt/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ meka ho asɛm no wɔ...
examples.note: Asɛm a ɛyɛ den ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. Wɔde 'I'd like' ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ.

examples.original: Let me begin with a quick introduction.
examples.phonetic: /let mi bɪˈɡɪn wɪð ə kwɪk ˌɪntrəˈdʌkʃən/
examples.translation: Ma me kyerɛkyerɛ, me bɛka ho asɛm no wɔ ɛha mu.
examples.note: Mfatoho bi ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. 'Let me' kyerɛ 'ma me'.

levels.label: Structuring ideas
levels.translation: Ma wɔde adwene wɔ mfatoho mma mu

examples.original: Firstly, let's look at the benefits.
examples.phonetic: /ˈfɜːrstli lets lʊk æt ðə ˈbenɪfɪts/
examples.translation: Pa ara, ma yehu nnwuma no.
examples.note: Wɔde 'firstly' ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. Ɛyɛ den paa wɔ 'first' mu.

examples.original: Secondly, I want to mention some challenges.
examples.phonetic: /ˈsekəndli aɪ wɑːnt tə ˈmenʃən sʌm ˈtʃælɪndʒɪz/
examples.translation: Ɛno ara, mepɛ sɛ mekyerɛkyerɛ nnwuma bi.
examples.note: Wɔde 'secondly' ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. Ma wɔde mfatoho a ɛyɛ den.

examples.original: Another important point is that...
examples.phonetic: /əˈnʌðər ɪmˈpɔːrtənt pɔɪnt ɪz ðæt/
examples.translation: Mfatoho bi nso ɛha na...
examples.note: Mfatoho bi ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. Ɛma wɔde mfatoho a ɛyɛ den.

examples.original: However, we must consider the costs.
examples.phonetic: /haʊˈevər wi mʌst kənˈsɪdər ðə kɔːsts/
examples.translation: Nanso, yɛnsɛ sɛ yɛhu nnipa no.
examples.note: 'However' kyerɛkyerɛ adwene a ɛyɛ den. Wɔ Hɔwyɛdeɛ mu, yɛde 'sin embargo'.

levels.label: Closing and concluding
levels.translation: Ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ ne ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ

examples.original: In conclusion, I'd like to summarize the main points.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn kənˈkluːʒən aɪd laɪk tə ˈsʌməraɪz ðə meɪn pɔɪnts/
examples.translation: Ma me kyerɛkyerɛ, mepɛ sɛ mekyerɛkyerɛ nnwuma a ɛyɛ den.
examples.note: Asɛm a ɛyɛ den ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. 'In conclusion' ɛyɛ den, nanso wɔde 'to sum up' wɔ mfatoho a ɛyɛ den mu.

examples.original: To wrap up, remember that every small action counts.
examples.phonetic: /tə ræp ʌp rɪˈmembər ðæt ˈevri smɔːl ˈækʃən kaʊnts/
examples.translation: Ma me kyerɛkyerɛ, monhu sɛ ɛyɛ den sɛ moyɛ.
examples.note: 'To wrap up' ɛyɛ den paa wɔ mfatoho a ɛyɛ den mu. De wɔde wɔ mfatoho a ɛyɛ den mu.

examples.original: Thank you for your attention.
examples.phonetic: /θæŋk ju fɔːr jʊər əˈtenʃən/
examples.translation: Meda wo ase wɔ mo asɛm mu.
examples.note: Asɛm a ɛyɛ den ma wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ. Wɔ Twirifɔdeɛ mu, wɔde 'your attention' (mo asɛm), ɛmmusɛ 'your time' wɔ ɛyi mu.
